aeronautics_utility_objects.ponder.share: Connect two pneumatic heads after the structures have been assembled.
The rod extends and retracts along the line between its two heads.
Target length and return force pull the moving end back toward the set distance.
Stretch resistance damps back-and-forth shaking along the rod axis.
Empty-hand right-click a linked head to open the pneumatic rod settings.
Expected Length changes the target height, and the real rod length follows.
With weak Return Force, a heavy load bottoms out the rod; more force lifts it back to the target.
For the same quick pull, higher Stretch Resistance makes the moving end respond slower.
Free mode lets the link slide instead of actively returning to the target.
A pneumatic regulator needs shaft input; redstone rewrites the target length through the configured range.
Place a pneumatic regulator behind a head, facing into it, to control that link.
Redstone signal selects the target length from the head's redstone range.
Shaft speed controls how quickly the rod transitions to the new target.
With no rotation, or when overstressed, the regulator stops commanding the head.
The hinge head stores a pin axis that is different from the rod facing.
After linking, the end may swing around that pin axis.
The hydraulic rod still controls only the distance between the two ends.
Both rods connect universal joint heads; the rod item decides which link is created.
Brass is a short elastic link; over-stretch it and the link turns red before it disconnects.
Andesite reaches much farther, but it keeps the linked rest length.
Moving either longer or shorter than that rest length can strain the joint until it breaks.
Both variants warn in red near their limits; keep linked bearings close to the length they were joined at.
Empty-hand right-click the bearing to assemble the attached blocks into a physical rotating structure.
The bearing reads the assembled structure's real angular speed.
That rotation is published from the rear shaft into the Create kinetic network.
Sneak-right-click the bearing to open its rotation bearing settings and tune Resistance.
It can also be used as a damped physical bearing, smoothing rotation before it reaches the shaft network.
message.aeronautics_utility_objects.wron: Both ends must be in the same dimension.
message.aeronautics_utility_objects.same: Use the same joint rod to finish this link.
Ends must be on different structures, or one may attach to the world.
message.aeronautics_utility_objects.stre: Blacklisted block detected: %s. Stress output limited to 40,000 SU.

tooltip.aeronautics_utility_objects.head: Links structures and passes motion across them.
The rod chooses whether the link is brass or andesite.
tooltip.aeronautics_utility_objects.rang: Long joint link with limited travel.
Elastic link that pulls stretched structures back.
tooltip.aeronautics_utility_objects.rod_: Right-click two joint heads to create a link.
tooltip.aeronautics_utility_objects.bras: Creates a brass universal joint link between universal joint heads.
tooltip.aeronautics_utility_objects.ande: Creates an andesite universal joint link between universal joint heads.
tooltip.aeronautics_utility_objects.rod_: Range 15 blocks. Travel over 1 block pulls back, 2.5 blocks breaks.
tooltip.aeronautics_utility_objects.hydr: Anchors a pneumatic rod. Aim at the rod body and right-click to tune it.
Normal rods can tune target length, return strength, and stretch resistance.
Andesite hinge head with one swinging axis; aim at the rod body to configure the rod.
The rod end may swing around the placed pin axis while the rod controls only its length.
Creates a configurable pneumatic link between two pneumatic heads.
Damping has 20 levels. Red levels are extra-strong and may be rough on light builds.
tooltip.aeronautics_utility_objects.crea: Creative rod: only target length is configurable, then enforced directly with a smooth but very stiff servo.
tooltip.aeronautics_utility_objects.hydr: Place behind a pneumatic head to override its target length.
Redstone signal sets target length; creative rods follow it as direct length targets.
Shaft speed controls how quickly the target length moves.
tooltip.aeronautics_utility_objects.damp: Outputs the attached structure's real rotation speed.
Damping rises hard at high speed; stress output is capped at 200,000 SU.
tooltip.aeronautics_utility_objects.stre: Detected %s. This bearing's stress output is limited to 40,000 SU.
Limits the oil volume passing through the directional valve and directly limits cylinder speed.
40 L/min retains rated speed; lower flow slows starting, reversing, and travel.
Limits maximum supply pressure and cylinder force.
Excess load naturally slows or stalls the cylinder.
Reduces back-and-forth shaking along the rod.
Higher values make fast stretching feel thicker and harder to shake.
Low is smoother; high is better for heavy machines but can fight light parts.
Red levels are the extra-strong range, not the everyday setting.
If a small build starts bouncing, lower this first.
Creative rods only use this length setting.
The rod directly moves toward this length, even against very heavy builds.
It is still smoothed a little so it does not snap instantly.
A pneumatic regulator is controlling this length right now.
Change the redstone signal or shaft speed at the regulator.
The length the rod tries to keep.
Shorter pulls the two ends together; longer pushes them apart.
The rod moves toward this length gradually instead of teleporting.
How strongly the rod corrects itself back to the expected length.
Higher values fix length errors faster and feel stiffer.
Too high can make small or loose builds bounce.
Maps redstone signal 0-15 into this length range.
The left handle is signal 0; the right handle is signal 15.
Works for both normal and creative pneumatic rods.
Target Length: the rod keeps trying to reach the set length.
Free: the rod can slide, but still keeps its safety range and shaking control.
Use Free when you want a sliding support instead of an active push-pull rod.
This setting is paused while Free mode is on.
tooltip.aeronautics_utility_objects.bras: A brass hydraulic hinge with configurable angular limits.
Right-click to set the minimum and maximum swing angle.
